newsitem.title: USA: Caribbean air hubs urged to compete with Miami.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean air hubs urged to compete with Miami.

text.p: Caribbean countries should try to develop airline hubs in their countries to grab more tourism and trade from Miami International Airport, a leading airline consultant told a conference here Tuesday.
"You can create a means to bypass Miami International Airport," said Robert Booth, president of Aviation Management Services, Miami.

"The way to develop more for the Caribbean is to develop more (air) service into Central and South America, create hubs into the Caribbean where people can hop on a plane (from the Caribbean) and go to inland destinations in the U.S.," Booth told those gathered at the Miami conference on the Caribbean and Latin America. Last year, 12.5 million visitors from Latin America visited the United States and 70 percent of them used Miami International, he said, "and most of them flew right over the Caribbean to get there."

Speaking on more general aviation issues, Booth said the rumored merger between Delta Air Lines Inc and Continental Airlines Inc would have "a dramatic impact in Latin America and the Caribbean because if this merger happens you will see a number of others in the making."
A Delta and Continental combination would create the biggest airline in the U.S.
If other large U.S. airlines were to follow the rumored Delta-Continental move, "this will create some real competition for (AMR Corp's ) American in Latin America and the Caribbean."
